values.name: __cve_id__
values.description: Vulnerability identifier carried by this case. Canonical form is a CVE id (e.g. CVE-2026-12345); operators MAY substitute a vendor advisory id or internal tracker id when no CVE has been assigned yet.

values.name: __report_source__
values.description: Where the disclosure originated. One of: researcher_report, vendor_advisory, cve_feed, internal_scanner.

values.name: __severity__
values.description: Triage severity derived from CVSS base / temporal score and EPSS exploit-probability band. One of: critical, high, medium, low, info.

values.name: __cvss_vector__
values.description: CVSS v3.1 / v4.0 vector string for the case (e.g. CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H). Populated by the triage step; carried into telemetry as part of the OCSF Vulnerability Finding payload.

values.name: __epss_score__
values.description: EPSS exploit-probability score (0.0 to 1.0, two decimal places) for the case at intake time. Populated by the triage step alongside the CVSS vector.

values.name: __asset_ref__
values.description: Reference into the operator's asset inventory for the affected component (asset id, SBOM component PURL, or repository path). Populated by the triage step against the operator's CMDB / SBOM service.

values.name: __actively_exploited__
values.description: Set by the CRA reporting-trigger step: true when the disclosure meets the CRA Article 14(1) actively-exploited definition (in-the-wild exploitation evidence) or the Article 14(3) severe-incident definition, in which case the regulator-notification chain fires ahead of the severity-keyed response so the 24h / 72h / 14d submission timing starts at the same instant the operator becomes aware.

values.name: __cve_id_canonical__
values.description: Canonical form of __cve_id__ written by canonicalize_case_field at intake (trimmed, upper-cased identifier scheme, stable across reporter formatting). The dedup key and every downstream case reference read this, never the raw __cve_id__.

values.name: __cvss__
values.description: Parsed CVSS handle (the CVSSScore model in primitives/cvss.py: the parsed vector, its computed base score and rating) produced from __cvss_vector__ at triage. The severity policy consumes this handle rather than re-parsing the vector string, so one deterministic parse feeds both severity and the regulator-notification chain.

values.name: __epss__
values.description: Parsed EPSS handle (the EPSSScore model in primitives/epss.py, Decimal-valued) produced from __epss_score__ at triage. Consumed by the severity policy alongside __cvss__.

values.name: __asset_context__
values.description: Business context for the affected component as read from the operator's inventory at triage (the BusinessContext model in primitives/severity.py). Distinct from __asset_ref__, which is the inventory reference this context was resolved from.

values.name: __severity_verdict__
values.description: Full severity verdict (SeverityVerdict) written by the severity policy: the severity plus the CVSS/EPSS factors and context flags that produced it. __severity__ carries the bare value for branch conditions; this carries the evidence.

values.name: __awareness_at__
values.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant the operator became aware. Anchors the Art. 14 24h and 72h clocks.

values.name: __exploitation_evidence__
values.description: Observed-exploitation evidence kind. Only observed exploitation engages Art. 14(1) — a high EPSS forecast does not.

values.name: __remedy_available_at__
values.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant a corrective or mitigating measure became available; anchors the 14-day final-report clock.

values.name: __notification_destinations__
values.description: Stage -> CSIRT/ENISA recipient. Fail-closed: no default endpoint ships.

values.name: __triaged_at__
values.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant triage completed; anchors every remediation deadline.

values.name: __cvd_sla_days__
values.description: Remediation window in days from the operator's documented CVD policy (CRA Annex I §2(5)).

values.name: __risk_accepted_by__
values.description: Named party accepting the residual risk on the None lane.

values.name: __risk_review_after_days__
values.description: Days until a risk acceptance must be revisited. No default — an acceptance without expiry becomes permanent by accident.

values.name: __cra_trigger_verdict__
values.description: CRA Art. 14 trigger verdict: whether reporting is owed and when each stage falls due.

values.name: __notification_chain_plan__
values.description: Ordered Art. 14 submission plan with resolved destinations.

values.name: __remediation_directive__
values.description: Remediation routing verdict from the lane that handled the case.

nodes.name: intake disclosure
nodes.notes: Receive an inbound vulnerability disclosure through the operator's coordinated disclosure channel (security.txt mailbox, advisory feed, CVE webhook, or internal scanner finding). Acknowledge the reporter where applicable per the operator's CVD policy and the CRA single-point-of-contact obligation, persist the raw submission, stamp __cve_id__ on the case, and emit an OCSF Vulnerability Finding event so downstream consumers (metrics, SIEM, ticketing) can pick the case up off a single telemetry channel.

nodes.name: triage and asset correlation

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.vuln_intake.primitives.severity import severity_policy
__severity_verdict__ = severity_policy(cvss=__cvss__, epss=__epss__, context=__asset_context__)

nodes.notes: Score the disclosure with CVSS (v3.1 / v4.0) and EPSS, derive the __severity__ band, and correlate the affected component against the operator's asset inventory and SBOM (PURL lookup). Outputs __severity__, __cvss_vector__, __epss_score__, and __asset_ref__. The SBOM lookup is the link between this playbook and the CRA Annex I §2(1) SBOM obligation — cases on releases that lack an SBOM record are counted against the releases-without-SBOM KRI so the gap is visible to the operator.

nodes.name: assess CRA reporting trigger
nodes.notes: Determine whether the disclosure trips the CRA Article 14(1) actively-exploited clock (in-the-wild exploitation evidence — public PoC, observed activity, vendor confirmation) or the Article 14(3) severe-incident clock. Sets __actively_exploited__. The incident-timeline-signals control is the contract for the timestamp set the regulator submissions consume.

nodes.name: actively exploited?
nodes.notes: Branch the case on the CRA reporting trigger. on_success: __actively_exploited__ is true and the regulator-notification chain fires ahead of the severity-keyed response so the CRA Article 14 24h / 72h / 14d clocks start at the operator's awareness timestamp. on_failure: the disclosure stays an internal-only case and routes directly to the severity switch.

nodes.name: regulator-notification chain (CRA Art. 14)
nodes.notes: Emit the CRA Article 14 regulator-notification chain: the 24-hour early-warning notification to the coordinator CSIRT + ENISA, the 72-hour notification with the corrective / mitigating measures the operator has taken or recommended, and the 14-day final report after a corrective measure becomes available. The submission-template control is the contract for the payload shape; the timeline-signals control is the contract for the timestamp set the submissions consume. Hands control to the severity switch so the technical response runs in series after the regulator notifications are dispatched.

nodes.name: route on severity
nodes.notes: Route to the technical-response branch keyed on __severity__. Each branch is a single response-routing action that ships the security update on the operator's SLA for that band, emits an advisory where applicable, and closes the case. The accept-risk branch documents the disposition without paging or scheduling a release.

nodes.name: response: critical — patch and advisory
nodes.notes: Critical-severity response: page the response team, ship the security update across affected releases for the duration of the support period free of charge per CRA Annex I §2(7), and emit a public advisory to users. Records the dissemination event against the patch-dissemination KPI and the critical-MTTR clock.

nodes.name: response: high — patch and advisory
nodes.notes: High-severity response: ship the security update on the operator's high-severity SLA and emit an advisory through the same dissemination channel as the critical branch. Same dissemination KPI; the response latency is measured against the patch-dissemination clock rather than the critical-band MTTR.

nodes.name: response: scheduled remediation
nodes.notes: Medium / low-severity response: schedule the security update on the operator's standard release cadence and roll the advisory into the next scheduled release note. The CRA Annex I §2(7) obligation to disseminate updates without undue delay is met by the operator's documented release SLA; the patch-dissemination clock measures whether that SLA is held.

nodes.name: response: accept risk

parameters.pythonCode:
from content.playbooks.vuln_intake.primitives.remediation import accept_risk
__remediation_directive__ = accept_risk(severity=__severity__, asset_criticality=__asset_context__.asset_criticality, triaged_at=__triaged_at__, accepted_by=__risk_accepted_by__, review_after_days=__risk_review_after_days__)

nodes.notes: Informational-severity response: record the disclosure on the case ledger with a documented accept-risk decision and close without paging or scheduling a release. The case still emits an OCSF Vulnerability Finding so the intake-aging KRI sees a closed disposition rather than an open backlog item.
